question: What is the relative charge of a proton and neutron?
solution:
The correct answer is __**+1 and 0 respectively.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Proton has a relative charge of +1, while neutron has a relative charge of 0.**
 
• The **charge** of an atom is determined by the** number of protons and electrons** it has.
 
• Protons and neutrons are both found in the** nucleus** of an atom.
 
• **The number of protons in an atom is the atomic number, while the total number of protons and neutrons is the mass number.**
 
• In an atom, the number of electrons is equal to the** number of protons, **making the atom electrically neutral.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A negatively charged subatomic particle known as an electron can be free (not bound) or bound to an atom.**
 
• The discovery of the electron is credited to **J. J. Thomson.**
 
• Each subshell that makes up the **KLMN shells **is only permitted a certain number of electrons.
 
• **The maximum number of electrons in the s subshell is two, the maximum number in the p subshell is six, the maximum number in the d subshell is ten, and the maximum number in the f subshell is fourteen.**
